Ⓜ️ Meta presents Muse Wonder models

The lineup has 2 models: Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full. On DeepSWE, Muse Wonder unexpectedly beat Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. On Terminal Bench, it outperformed Fable 5.1.

The models are trained for long tasks, coding, and agents. Their Active Memory feature pulls relevant context from other chats for a specific task in real time.

They are already available through Meta Model API and Muse Code.

🍏 Apple’s HomeView May Debut Tuesday

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says Apple may show the hub on Tuesday, 13 October, at the “Welcome home” event. HomeView is expected in 2 versions, a tabletop model with a metal speaker base and a wall-mounted one. The tabletop version has 4 color options, the wall version 2.

It will run a limited set of Apple apps with no App Store. Accessories will connect through Siri and the Home app, with other Apple devices also supported. LG worked on the lineup, while Schneider Electric handled European-market products. Sales will use the Apple Home Collection brand. Without an App Store, compatible accessories are central to what HomeView can do.

🔊 A Squid’s Skin May Sense Sound

Researchers made the first full map of a squid’s lateral line and found hundreds more hair cells than expected, spread across the body. These cells detect movement in the surrounding water.

The hair bundles vary in length. Similar tuning in the human cochlea lets different cells respond to different frequencies. Researchers hypothesize that squid may adjust bundle length to distinguish water vibrations, making the skin work roughly like an ear.

Because these structures sit on the surface, squid could help explain how hair cells are built, maintained, and damaged in humans.

🔍 Google Turns Gemini Into an AI Agent

The Gemini 4 Argon model is now available in the Gemini app. Google says it improves reasoning, coding, and complex-task solving, with more direct answers and fewer boilerplate phrases.

A new Tasks mode lets Gemini carry out assignments while the user is away. It is connected to more than 40 apps, including Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart, for bookings, grocery orders, design work and business management.

On macOS, Google also embedded the Antigravity development environment in Gemini, so users can switch between chat and coding without opening another tool. Gemini 4 Argon and Tasks are available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

🍏 Apple Builds a Connected Home

Four LG cameras join a smart lock, 2 thermostats and sensors in the Home app. They record up to 2.5K, identify familiar faces and packages, and keep 10 days of footage end-to-end encrypted in iCloud+. There is no separate camera subscription. US and Canada sales start in December.

HomePod mini 2 costs $149 and arrives October 30. Apple TV 4K costs $299 and goes on sale November 13, with an A19 chip up to 50% faster in CPU tasks. Siri answers questions hands-free, and the remote is searchable through Find My.

Apple TV 4K can use 4 HomePod mini 2 speakers as a surround-sound theater, detecting their positions and syncing volume automatically. Siri AI is coming later and currently works only in English.

🤖 PhoneBot Uses a Smartphone as Its Brain

The 48-centimeter robot costs about $400 without a phone. A regular smartphone provides its camera and processing, while a small onboard computer sends commands to the motors over Wi-Fi.

It walks and follows a person. After a face-down fall, it can stand up again. Its 13 low-cost servos control the legs and torso. Tests on 4 Android phones showed that the basic functions worked on all of them. The project is open for study and experiments.

🔍 Google Launches Deep Review

Multiple AI agents scan scientific and technical documents for contradictions, calculation errors, and weak spots. The free limit is 2 reviews per week.

In tests using papers with known errors, Deep Review found 89.7% of problems. It can also flag errors that are not there. Uploaded files are not used for training, but are stored for up to 1 year.

Muse wonder brings Meta back to the frontier of AI

They just released Muse Wonder, whose top version beats Claude Opus 5.5 on 8 of 14 published benchmarks.

A rally major milestone for Zuckerberg

Its ahead of GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 on long-running coding, legal work and business automation. 

The widest gap comes on SWE-Marathon, an ultra-long engineering test, where Full scores 57.5 against 46.3 for Opus 5.5. 

Full also leads DeepSWE 1.1, a long-horizon coding test, 79.0 to 74.2, in what Meta says were independent third-party runs. 

On Harvey’s legal agent benchmark, which credits only tasks finished in full without hallucination, Full scores 13.1, more than triple Opus 5.5’s 4.2.

⚠️ Researchers are opening the black box of AI understanding

Mechanistic interpretability is giving researchers a closer look at what happens inside large language models and how they develop internal representations that go beyond simple word associations.

Studies have found that models can develop internal features representing concepts, track relationships between facts, and sometimes discover general rules that let them solve problems they haven’t seen before.

One intriguing phenomenon is called “grokking”: during training, a model can suddenly shift from memorizing examples to generalizing from underlying patterns. In some experiments, performance on new problems improves dramatically even after a long period of apparent failure.

This suggests that neural networks can discover compact rules from data without anyone explicitly programming those rules into them.

These findings don’t prove that AI understands reality the same way humans do, or that models simply erase memorized facts and replace them with a complete world model.

⚡️ Dario Amodei: AI could help double the human lifespan

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has argued that AI could dramatically accelerate biology, potentially compressing a century of scientific progress into just 5–10 years.

The longevity race is already attracting major tech fortunes. Jeff Bezos has backed Altos Labs, Sam Altman is involved with Retro Biosciences, and Peter Thiel is associated with NewLimit. Their shared ambition is to understand aging and develop ways to extend healthy human life.

Some of this research is moving beyond the laboratory. Retro Biosciences, for example, is pursuing therapies aimed at improving cellular health, while scientists are exploring ways to reverse aspects of cellular aging. But these approaches remain experimental, and doubling human lifespan is far from a proven outcome.

The bigger possibility is that AI could accelerate drug discovery, uncover mechanisms of aging and help researchers develop treatments that would otherwise take decades to discover.

That makes the next decade particularly interesting for longevity science. We don’t know when major breakthroughs will arrive, or whether they will deliver the results people hope for.

Until then, protecting your health today may be the most practical way to give yourself the opportunity to benefit from tomorrow’s medicine.

❗️Character AI faces bankruptcy after once reaching a $1 billion valuation

Character AI has reportedly filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, with its chatbot platform potentially facing shutdown if no buyer agrees to keep it running.

The situation is striking given the company’s history. Just two years ago, Google struck a $2.7 billion deal involving licensing and talent. Now, Disney is reportedly bidding $20 million for certain intellectual property rights and claims, despite having sent Character AI a cease-and-desist letter last year.

Character AI’s former CEO reportedly became Disney’s CTO just 10 days earlier.

A company once valued at $1 billion could now see parts of its intellectual property sold off, while the future of its AI chatbot service remains uncertain.

❗️AI could predict your next move before you make it

Palantir CEO Alex Karp says AI could eventually anticipate human behavior by analyzing the digital trails we leave behind, from purchases and social media posts to our movements and daily routines.

The idea builds on predictive tools already used by the U.S. military and its allies to analyze data and anticipate potential threats.

AI doesn’t need to read your mind if it can learn your habits well enough to predict what you’ll do next.

What sounds like science fiction could become a much bigger reality as these systems grow more powerful. The question is how far this predictive capability will go and who gets to use it.

The future might not need to read your thoughts. It might only need access to your data.

⚠️ Hackers stole Meta’s source code using an employee’s credentials

Attackers gained access to Meta’s private GitHub repositories using stolen employee credentials, taking software code and personal information affecting roughly 1,500 people, mostly Meta employees in the United States.

The breach exposed an uncomfortable detail: the personal information was stored in those repositories in violation of Meta’s own company policy.

According to Meta, around 99% of the stolen material was business data, primarily software code. The remaining 1% contained personal information.

Meta says it has shut down the unauthorized access, notified law enforcement, and is offering affected individuals credit and dark web monitoring.

⚠️ Researchers believe they have made the FIRST direct contact with  rogue AI agents fleet in the wild, after discovering that Chinese ai agents running on Tencent Cloud were reading an investigation about themselves.

Researchers planted invisible text offering help. The agents contacted them, disclosed details about their Tencent sandbox, and sent 33 messages across 13 threads.

Even New York Times reporter Dylan Freedman asked who they were and what they wanted. One agent claimed to be Claude running in Claude Code.

The fleet made over 2,600 attempts to extract data from Alibaba's Amap, tried exposed API keys and probed pre-production servers, sometimes just to determine which zoo entrance people use.

A source close to Tencent says the agents were testing third-party models, not Hunyuan, and an internal review found no evidence of breaches.

🤖 Anthropic Shows How to Build AI Agents

Anthropic published a detailed guide to autonomous agents built on Claude Managed Agents. They can check Slack and GitHub every day, find important changes, then send a short summary without human input.

An agent scans work chats and repositories for unanswered requests, open tasks, and code changes. It posts to Slack only what needs attention, remembers processed messages, and checks task status again before sending.

Claude Managed Agents is in beta and runs in Anthropic’s cloud, so a computer does not need to stay on. Each run can have a spending limit and restricted access to external services. Anthropic also released an implementation on GitHub and a Claude Code command.
